newsitem.title: USA: Beazer Homes USA says July new orders grew.
newsitem.headline: Beazer Homes USA says July new orders grew.

text.p: Beazer Homes USA Inc said Wednesday that despite lower third quarter earnings, its new order growth accelerated in all states in July and it sees significant earnings improvement in the future from new subdivisions.
Earnings for the third quarter ended June 30 were $0.40 per share, compared with $0.53 for the third quarter of 1996.
Beazer said it had 1,594 new orders for the quarter, up from 1,506 new orders in the comparable quarter of the prior year.

"Although our earnings for the quarter were down as a result of lower revenues, we are extremely pleased with the recent increase that we have seen in new orders. New orders increased 5.8 percent for the quarter ended June 30, 1997. In addition, with recent interest rate declines, we have seen our new order growth accelerating in all states in July," said chief executive Ian McCarthy.
McCarthy said the company was experiencing the lower volume and earnings that resulted from a reduction in the number of active subdivisions in late 1996 and early 1997.

"Since December 31, 1996, we have opened over 50 new subdivisions, including 16 in our largest market, Phoenix. These new subdivisions are producing the accelerating order trend that we believe will produce significant earnings improvements in future quarters," McCarthy said.
Gross margin, before amortization of previously capitalized interest fell to 15.2 percent in the quarter from 15.3 percent in the third quarter of 1996.
Beazer attributed the decline in gross margin primarily to Nevada operations.
The company said gross margin in Nevada is improving and should show further improvement in future quarters.
Separately, Beazer said it was expanding its revolving credit facility from $150 million to $200 million.
